result.title: LEAF-Mamba: Feature Adaptation and Fusion for Whole Slide Image Analysis
result.summary: Whole slide image (WSI) analysis enables computational diagnosis and prognosis, but gigapixel images and limited annotations make slide-level learning challenging. Multiple instance learning addresses this task by aggregating patch representations from frozen pretrained encoders. Recently, Mamba has enabled efficient modeling of long patch sequences. However, task supervision alone does not explicitly constrain information recovery during feature adaptation, while Mamba couples local processing with long-range propagation rather than retaining separate representations for fusion. Motivated by these challenges, we introduce LEAF-Mamba, a framework that jointly addresses latent evidence adaptation and fusion for frozen-feature WSI analysis. A reconstruction-regularized adapter learns compact, task-specific representations while reconstructing the input features. Parallel Mamba and convolutional streams then capture long-range dependencies and sequence-local interactions, with an input-dependent gate modulating their joint representation before slide-level pooling. Experiments across feature extractors demonstrate improved average performance over strong MIL baselines in both diagnostic classification and survival prediction. Component analyses further support the contributions of adaptation and fusion. These findings highlight the value of jointly designing feature transformation and contextual aggregation to translate pretrained representations into effective slide-level predictions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LEAF-Mamba，用于全切片病理图像分析：在冻结编码器特征上以重建正则化适配器学习紧凑的任务表示，并联 Mamba 与卷积分支分别建模长程与局部交互，再经输入相关门控融合并做切片级池化，在诊断分类和生存预测上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用重建约束防止特征适配中信息丢失」与多路表示门控融合，可能为 LVR 中视觉信息坍缩、旁路及多种 latent 状态组合提供可供核查的监督与融合线索，但实验限于 WSI，迁移性尚待验证。
